haiku-low.q1: Three consecutive breach evaluations (over 2% 5xx, at least 500 requests) while no incident is open for that service and rule.
haiku-low.q2: The breach is added to the open incident with no new page sent.
haiku-low.q3: Ten consecutive clear evaluations (under 1% 5xx, at least 500 requests) resolve it, cancel pending escalation, and send resolved notices. A later breach opens a new incident.
haiku-low.q4: Primary is paged first. After 5 minutes without ack, secondary is paged. After another 5 minutes, the engineering manager, the last level.
haiku-low.q5: An SMS is sent. The escalation clock does not wait, and each failure is logged in page_log. If both fail, escalation continues on schedule and the failure is flagged.
haiku-low.q6: Everyone paged on that incident gets a resolved notice (push, SMS if push fails). Pending escalation timers are cancelled.
haiku-low.q7: Streak counters are stored in the incidents table. A non-breach resets the breach streak; an evaluation at or above 1% resets the clear streak. Low traffic pauses both.
haiku-low.q8: Evaluations have a unique key on (service, rule, minute), so the first write wins. A partial unique index allows only one open incident per service and rule.
haiku-low.q9: A timer queue fires each step, and evaluators sweep for overdue next_escalation_at. The step proceeds only if the incident is still open and unacked, after claiming the level's page_log row.
haiku-low.q10: The paging provider calls the webhook with incident id and engineer. The system sets acked_at and acked_by (first ack wins) and cancels the pending escalation timer.
haiku-low.q11: The rota is looked up from the schedule service each time someone is paged, not once at incident start. If it is down, the stored snapshot is used.

sonnet.q1: 3 consecutive breach evaluations (each: over 2% 5xx with at least 500 requests in the trailing 5-minute window) and no open incident for that (service, rule) pair.
sonnet.q2: The breach is added to the open incident and no new page is sent; a second incident can't open because of the partial unique index on open incidents per (service, rule). Escalation continues on its timers unless acked.
sonnet.q3: 10 consecutive clear evaluations (under 1% 5xx, at least 500 requests) resolve it. After resolving, a new breach opens a new incident (presumably after the usual 3-breach streak; the document only says a new breach opens a new incident).
sonnet.q4: Primary immediately when the incident opens; secondary after 5 minutes with no ack; engineering manager (last level) after another 5 minutes with no ack.
sonnet.q5: If push fails, an SMS is sent. Escalation doesn't wait: the next timer is set right after the send attempts whatever the result. Failures are recorded in page_log. If both push and SMS fail, the incident still escalates on schedule and the failure is logged and flagged for follow-up.
sonnet.q6: Everyone who was paged on the incident gets a resolved notice (push, SMS if push fails). The pending escalation timer is cancelled.
sonnet.q7: In the incidents table in Postgres (breach and clear streak counters). A breach streak is reset by any evaluation that is not a breach, including middle band; the clear streak is reset by an evaluation at or above 1%. Low-traffic windows pause (don't add to or reset) the streaks. The document does not say what happens to the counters when an incident has not yet been created (the incident row is inserted at the 3rd breach), so the pre-incident storage location is NOT STATED.
sonnet.q8: Both write to evaluations with a unique key (service, rule, minute); first write wins, second ignored, so a minute is not double-counted. A partial unique index on open incidents per (service, rule) prevents two open incidents. They coordinate through Postgres with no leader election.
sonnet.q9: A timer from the timer queue fires (incident, next level), or the evaluator's sweep of incidents whose next_escalation_at has passed. The step reads incident state from Postgres: if still open and not acked, it claims the page_log row for that level (unique key on incident and level; if the insert fails, someone else claimed it and it does nothing) and then pages; if already acked or resolved, it does nothing.
sonnet.q10: The engineer taps Acknowledge in the paging app; the paging provider calls the incident manager's webhook with incident id and engineer. It sets acked_at and acked_by in Postgres (first ack wins) and cancels the pending escalation timer.
sonnet.q11: At the time of each page, not when the incident starts: the system asks the schedule service who is on call right now for that level each time it pages. If the schedule service is down, it uses the rota snapshot stored on the incident from the last successful lookup and retries in the background.
sonnet.q12: It loops over each person paged on the incident; the document doesn't explicitly say where the list comes from, though page_log holds one row per page attempt with incident id, level and recipient. The lookup mechanism is NOT STATED explicitly.
